requirements.title: ASSIGNMENT generic specifications require subroutines referenced as defined assignments
requirements.definition: An ASSIGNMENT(=) generic specification names subroutines that can be referenced as defined assignments; defined assignment can be generic over more than one subroutine.

pending.assignment-specifics-subroutines: PENDING executable plan: INTERFACE ASSIGNMENT(=) names subroutine assign_int_to_box; assigning integer 6 to TYPE(box) variable initialized with component -66 sets component 106, proving the subroutine is referenced as defined assignment.
pending.assignment-generic-multiple-subroutines: PENDING executable plan adds assign_real_to_box; integer assignment yields component 106 and real assignment with 2.5 yields component 250, each from distinct sentinels -66 and -77.
pending.assignment-subroutine-positive-control: PENDING source-control plan mutates one assignment specific to a function returning TYPE(box), while the conforming control keeps a subroutine and exact component result 106; no diagnostic is claimed for the prose mutation.

requirements.title: Defined assignment subroutines have two suitable dummy arguments and differ from intrinsic assignment
requirements.definition: Each defined assignment subroutine has exactly two nonoptional dummy data objects; the first has INTENT(OUT) or INTENT(INOUT), the second has INTENT(IN) or VALUE, and the pair extends or redefines assignment by rank difference, nonconforming declared type/kind parameters, or a derived-type first argument.

pending.assignment-exactly-two-dummies: PENDING source-control plan contrasts the conforming two-dummy assign_int_to_box with one-dummy and three-dummy mutations; the executable control observes box%value==106 after starting at -66.
pending.assignment-dummies-nonoptional-data: PENDING source-control plan changes only the second dummy to OPTIONAL and separately to a dummy procedure; the positive control keeps a nonoptional integer data dummy and exact component 106.
pending.assignment-first-intent-out-or-inout: PENDING source-control plan uses one subroutine with INTENT(OUT) first dummy and one with INTENT(INOUT) first dummy; both set distinct nondefault components, while an INTENT(IN) mutation carries no diagnostic claim here.
pending.assignment-second-intent-in-or-value: PENDING source-control plan uses INTENT(IN) and VALUE second dummies in separate conforming assignments; exact components 106 and 206 prove the subroutine received the right-hand value.
pending.assignment-rank-type-kind-or-derived-con: PENDING positive source plan covers derived first argument with scalar integer right-hand side and a separate array-rank differing assignment; exact component or array element sentinels show extension rather than intrinsic scalar assignment.

requirements.title: Defined assignment is a subroutine reference with left and right sides as actual arguments
requirements.definition: A defined assignment is treated as a subroutine reference: the left-hand side is the first argument, the right-hand side enclosed in parentheses is the second argument, applicable actual-argument restrictions apply, and the ASSIGNMENT generic specification extends or redefines assignment.

pending.defined-assignment-invokes-subroutine: PENDING executable plan: assignment box_var = 6 calls assign_int_to_box and sets box_var%value from sentinel -66 to exact 106; direct subroutine call is the control and removing the interface leaves no claimed defined-assignment effect.
pending.lhs-first-argument: PENDING executable plan initializes two TYPE(box) variables with -1 and -2, assigns only lhs = 6, and observes only lhs%value becomes 106 while the other variable remains -2.
pending.rhs-parenthesized-second-argument: PENDING source-control plan uses a second dummy with INTENT(IN) scalar integer and observes exact value 6 inside the assignment through component 106; pointer or allocatable right-hand attribute tests stay with actual-argument rules.
pending.assignment-actual-restrictions: PENDING source-control plan maps any invalid left-hand or right-hand expression to the independently registered actual-argument or variable-definition restriction reached by the corresponding dummy.
pending.assignment-extended-or-redefined: PENDING executable plan contrasts intrinsic integer assignment i=6 yielding 6 with defined TYPE(box)=6 yielding component 106, proving the generic specification changes assignment semantics only for the registered pair.
